1	"""Chinese Bigram Confusion Disambiguation Memory.
2	
3	The base confusion_disambiguation_memory uses an ASCII-only tokenizer
4	(re.findall r"[A-Za-z0-9]+") which captures only numbers and Latin tokens
5	from Chinese legal text. This makes Jaccard similarity near-zero for all
6	pairs, rendering the confusion-disambiguation selection algorithm random.
7	
8	This system replaces the tokenizer with Chinese character bigrams + ASCII
9	tokens so that Jaccard similarity captures semantic content of the case
10	facts. Everything else — the confusion matrix, the disambiguation selection
11	algorithm, the prompt template — is unchanged.
12	
13	Hypothesis (falsifiable): replacing ASCII-only tokenization with Chinese
14	bigrams will increase the benchmark val accuracy above 26% by enabling the
15	confusion-disambiguation mechanism to retrieve semantically relevant examples.
16	"""
17	
18	import json
19	import re
20	from collections import defaultdict
21	from typing import Any
22	
23	from ..llm import LLMCallable
24	from ..memory_system import MemorySystem, extract_json_field
25	
26	PROMPT_TEMPLATE = """Solve the problem below based on the examples provided.
27	
28	{examples_section}
29	
30	**Problem:**
31	{input}
32	
33	**Instructions:**
34	- Follow the patterns shown in the examples above
35	- Respond in JSON format
36	
37	{{"reasoning": "[your reasoning]", "final_answer": "[your answer]"}}"""
38	
39	MAX_CHARS = 30000
40	_TOP_CANDIDATE_LABELS = 3
41	_DISAMBIG_PER_CONFUSION = 2
42	
43	
44	def _tokenize(text: str) -> frozenset:
45	    """Chinese bigram + ASCII tokenizer.
46	
47	    Extracts consecutive pairs of Chinese characters (bigrams) plus ASCII
48	    alphanumeric tokens. On a typical Chinese legal case, this produces
49	    ~80-150 tokens vs. ~2-8 for the ASCII-only baseline.
50	    """
51	    ascii_tokens = re.findall(r"[A-Za-z0-9]+", text.lower())
52	    chars = re.findall(r"[一-鿿]", text)
53	    bigrams = [chars[i] + chars[i + 1] for i in range(len(chars) - 1)]
54	    return frozenset(ascii_tokens + bigrams)
55	
56	
57	def _jaccard(a: frozenset, b: frozenset) -> float:
58	    if not a and not b:
59	        return 0.0
60	    return len(a & b) / len(a | b)
61	
62	
63	class ChineseBigramConfusionMemory(MemorySystem):
64	    """Confusion-disambiguation with Chinese bigram similarity.
65	
66	    Identical selection algorithm to ConfusionDisambiguationMemory but with
67	    a tokenizer that produces meaningful Jaccard scores for Chinese text.
68	    """
69	
70	    def __init__(self, llm: LLMCallable):
71	        super().__init__(llm)
72	        self.examples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
73	        self.confusion: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
74	
75	    def _scored(self, query: str) -> list[tuple[float, int, dict]]:
76	        """Return all examples sorted by descending Jaccard similarity."""
77	        q_tok = _tokenize(query)
78	        result = [
79	            (_jaccard(q_tok, ex["tokens"]), idx, ex)
80	            for idx, ex in enumerate(self.examples)
81	        ]
82	        result.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], x[1]), reverse=True)
83	        return result
84	
85	    def _confusion_targets_for(self, labels: list[str]) -> list[str]:
86	        """Return labels most frequently confused with the given candidates."""
87	        label_set = set(labels)
88	        counts: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
89	        for lbl in labels:
90	            row = self.confusion.get(lbl, {})
91	            for actual, cnt in row.items():
92	                if actual not in label_set:
93	                    counts[actual] += cnt
94	        return [lbl for lbl, _ in sorted(counts.items(), key=lambda x: (-x[1], x[0]))]
95	
96	    def _build_parts(self, query: str) -> list[str]:
97	        """Select a mix of disambiguation and similarity examples within char budget."""
98	        if not self.examples:
99	            return []
100	
101	        ranked = self._scored(query)
102	
103	        top_labels = [ex["target"] for _, _, ex in ranked[:_TOP_CANDIDATE_LABELS]]
104	        confused_with = self._confusion_targets_for(top_labels)
105	
106	        parts: list[str] = []
107	        used_indices: set[int] = set()
108	        total_chars = 0
109	
110	        def try_add(idx: int, ex: dict) -> bool:
111	            nonlocal total_chars
112	            if idx in used_indices:
113	                return False
114	            q = ex.get("raw_question", ex["input"])
115	            part = f"Q: {q}\nA: {ex['target']}"
116	            if total_chars + len(part) + 2 > MAX_CHARS:
117	                return False
118	            parts.append(part)
119	            used_indices.add(idx)
120	            total_chars += len(part) + 2
121	            return True
122	
123	        if confused_with:
124	            disambig_labels_needed = set(confused_with[:_TOP_CANDIDATE_LABELS])
125	            per_label_disambig: dict[str, list[tuple[float, int, dict]]] = defaultdict(list)
126	            for score, idx, ex in ranked:
127	                if ex["target"] in disambig_labels_needed:
128	                    per_label_disambig[ex["target"]].append((score, idx, ex))
129	
130	            for _round in range(_DISAMBIG_PER_CONFUSION):
131	                for lbl in confused_with[:_TOP_CANDIDATE_LABELS]:
132	                    pool = per_label_disambig.get(lbl, [])
133	                    for score, idx, ex in pool:
134	                        if idx not in used_indices:
135	                            try_add(idx, ex)
136	                            break
137	
138	        for _, idx, ex in ranked:
139	            if total_chars >= MAX_CHARS:
140	                break
141	            try_add(idx, ex)
142	
143	        return parts
144	
145	    def predict(self, input: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:
146	        parts = self._build_parts(input)
147	        examples_section = "\n\n".join(parts)
148	        prompt = PROMPT_TEMPLATE.format(
149	            examples_section=examples_section,
150	            input=input,
151	        )
152	        response = self.call_llm(prompt)
153	        answer = extract_json_field(response, "final_answer")
154	        return answer, {
155	            "full_response": response,
156	            "num_examples": len(self.examples),
157	            "num_selected": len(parts),
158	            "num_confusion_pairs": sum(len(v) for v in self.confusion.values()),
159	        }
160	
161	    def learn_from_batch(self, batch_results: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
162	        for r in batch_results:
163	            raw_q = r.get("raw_question", r["input"])
164	            ex: dict[str, Any] = {
165	                "input": r["input"],
166	                "target": r["ground_truth"],
167	                "tokens": _tokenize(raw_q),
168	            }
169	            if "raw_question" in r:
170	                ex["raw_question"] = r["raw_question"]
171	            self.examples.append(ex)
172	
173	            if not r.get("was_correct", True):
174	                pred = r.get("prediction", "")
175	                gt = r["ground_truth"]
176	                if pred and pred != gt:
177	                    self.confusion[pred][gt] += 1
178	
179	    def get_context_length(self) -> int:
180	        return sum(len(p) + 2 for p in self._build_parts(""))
181	
182	    def get_state(self) -> str:
183	        serialisable = [
184	            {k: (sorted(v) if isinstance(v, frozenset) else v) for k, v in ex.items()}
185	            for ex in self.examples
186	        ]
187	        confusion_plain = {k: dict(v) for k, v in self.confusion.items()}
188	        return json.dumps({
189	            "examples": serialisable,
190	            "confusion": confusion_plain,
191	        }, indent=2)
192	
193	    def set_state(self, state: str) -> None:
194	        data = json.loads(state)
195	        self.examples = []
196	        for ex in data.get("examples", []):
197	            restored = dict(ex)
198	            if "tokens" in restored and isinstance(restored["tokens"], list):
199	                restored["tokens"] = frozenset(restored["tokens"])
200	            else:
201	                raw_q = restored.get("raw_question", restored.get("input", ""))
202	                restored["tokens"] = _tokenize(raw_q)
203	            self.examples.append(restored)
204	
205	        self.confusion = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
206	        for pred, actuals in data.get("confusion", {}).items():
207	            for actual, cnt in actuals.items():
208	                self.confusion[pred][actual] = cnt
209
